recent_articles.title: Governor, CM extend Easter greetings - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala’s Governor**, **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan**, and **Leader of the Opposition V D Satheesan** extended Easter greetings to the state's people, emphasizing themes of hope, love, and resilience. **Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar** noted that Easter reminds us of the enduring power of hope and compassion through Jesus' resurrection.  **Vijayan** highlighted the triumph of goodness over adversity and called for unity and peace during challenging times.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: NDA candidate alleges deal between CM, Opposition leader in Dharmadam, Peravur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K. Ranjith**, the NDA candidate in Dharmadam, accused **Pinarayi Vijayan** and **V.D. Satheesan** of a deal during a media address in Kannur.  Ranjith claimed the electoral contest was between the Left Democratic Front and the NDA, with the United Democratic Front candidate's campaign being minimal. He demanded the Election Commission verify campaign spending for **Pinarayi Vijayan**'s Dharmadam campaign and stated the NDA would file a formal complaint regarding the expenses.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: LDF, UDF in a tight fight in Kuttiyadi; NDA hoping to make a change - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K.P. Kunhammed Kutty**, the incumbent **LDF** candidate for Kuttiyadi, is seeking re-election after a narrow victory in 2021.  He highlights development projects such as new school buildings and infrastructure improvements to his constituency.  His rival, **Parakkal Abdulla**, from the **IUML**, claims an anti-incumbency wave against the state government will impact the election.  The **BJP**'s **Ramadas Manaleri** is also campaigning in Kuttiyadi, emphasizing the lack of progress under the current government and focusing on projects implemented by the **Narendra Modi** administration at the center. The outcome remains uncertain as campaigning nears its end.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections 2026: allegations of Congress-BJP nexus absurd, says Chennithala - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ramesh Chennithala**, a senior Congress leader and UDF candidate, refuted allegations of a nexus between the Congress and the BJP in the ongoing Kerala election. He claimed that both **Narendra Modi** and **Pinarayi Vijayan** share a common aim to achieve their respective political goals.  Chennithala also accused the CPI(M) and the BJP of colluding in 2021, alleging this collusion is being used as a cover for current accusations against the Congress. He emphasized that the Congress's main rivals are the BJP nationally and the CPI(M) in Kerala, while highlighting their plans to address issues like the elderly population and welfare pensions.  Chennithala dismissed criticism of the Oommen Chandy government's handling of welfare pensions and pledged to implement the five guarantees promised by the party in other states if elected.

recent_articles.title: Kerala elections: Rahul Gandhi sharpens attack on LDF and NDA, accuses both fronts of striking ‘covert deal’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, intensified his campaign in Kerala on Saturday (April 4, 2026), accusing the **CPI(M)-led LDF government** of a "hidden partnership" with the BJP and the RSS.  He criticized the lack of federal investigations into the alleged theft of gold from the Sabarimala temple and the failure to protect farmers.  Gandhi also accused Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** of compromising India's sovereignty and exerting control over the state government. The rally, attended by several prominent leaders, saw a massive turnout in support of UDF candidates across five constituencies.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Satheesan says ‘paid’ surveys don’t reflect public mood, calls BJP ‘a wolf in sheep’s clothing’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, Leader of the Opposition in Kerala, criticized recent opinion polls as "fabricated" and lacking credibility, claiming they are attempts to create an artificial perception of a close race between parties. He expressed confidence that the **Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF)** will secure over 100 seats and form the government.  **Suresh Gopi**, MP, was also cited as expressing concerns about the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) and its potential to weaken institutions. Satheesan further criticized Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for alleged violence against opposition supporters and accused the BJP of targeting minority groups.

recent_articles.title: Pinarayi Vijayan slams T.K. Govindan, backs P.K. Shyamala in Taliparamba - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** criticized former **CPI(M) leader T.K. Govindan**, accusing him of opportunism and betrayal ahead of the Taliparamba assembly election.  **Mr. Vijayan** stated that Mr. Govindan's move to run as an independent candidate was driven by seat ambitions rather than ideological differences, calling it a breach of trust beyond mere disagreement. **Mr. Vijayan** also criticized the **United Democratic Front (UDF)** for supporting Mr. Govindan and endorsed LDF candidate P.K. Shyamala, highlighting her experience and public service record.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections: Pinarayi Vijayan slams Telangana CM Revanth Reddy for ‘disparaging’ State - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, **Kerala Chief Minister**, criticized **Revanth Reddy**, the **Telangana** counterpart, for disparaging Kerala's development and social security programs.  Mr. Reddy had made remarks comparing Kerala to a declining state, but Mr. Vijayan countered with data from **NITI Aayog**, highlighting Kerala's low poverty rates and high literacy rates. He also pointed out the contrast between Telangana's defaulting on salaries and pensions and Kerala's robust social welfare programs, including its LIFE Housing Mission.  Mr. Vijayan concluded that Mr. Reddy's attempts to compare the two states were "indecorous" and misleading.

recent_articles.title: From selfies to slogan: how Instagram is becoming India’s newest political battleground - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ankit Pandey** posted a video of men praying on the railway platform, sparking outrage and leading to increased political content consumption on **Instagram**.  Political parties are increasingly using short-form videos, memes, and AI-generated content to reach young voters. This trend has led to concerns about misinformation and censorship as governments attempt to control the spread of political messaging on the platform. While some creators see opportunities for engagement and influence, others worry about the impact of short attention spans and the potential for disinformation.  Despite the rise in political content, many voters still rely on longer-form videos like YouTube for their political information.

recent_articles.title: On the campaign trail with K.C. Venugopal: When campaign gathers national and global vibes on north Kerala coast - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **K.C. Venugopal**, a key figure in the **Congress** party, is actively campaigning for the upcoming Kerala Assembly election. He has been coordinating with the opposition to stall changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act and leading rallies across the state.  Venugopal emphasizes his party's partnership with the Left while maintaining rivalry within the state, highlighting issues like the impact of the US-Israel conflict on fishermen and criticizing the CPI(M)'s alliance with the BJP. He also asserts that the Congress is the true Left in Kerala and aims to unseat the incumbent Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Chief Minister campaigns for LDF candidates in Kozhikode - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** campaigned for **LDF** candidates in Kozhikode district, focusing on development initiatives and criticizing the **Congress-led UDF** and **BJP**.  He addressed rallies in various locations, including Beypore, Kunnamangalam, and Kozhikode beach. The manifesto outlined 60 programs with 950 proposals, including poverty eradication, increased welfare pensions, and universal health coverage.

recent_articles.title: Lyricist Fr. Justin Panakkal passes away - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Fr. Justin Panakkal**, a lyricist and writer, passed away in Kochi on Thursday (April 2).  The funeral will be held on April 6 at Manjummal. **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** expressed condolences for the loss.

recent_articles.title: Revanth campaigns in Kerala, says LDF and BJP have secret pact - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **A. Revanth Reddy**, Chief Minister of **Telangana**, campaigned in Kerala for the Congress party, accusing both the **BJP** and the **LDF** of engaging in a "secret pact."  He criticized the **LDF** government for stalling national development projects and accused the **Centre** of misusing agencies like the ED and CBI.  **Reddy** also praised Kerala's achievements but expressed confidence that a Congress government would lead to progress.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election 2026: Pinarayi Vijayan slams ‘Congress-BJP nexus’ over G. Sudhakaran’s rebel bid in Ambalappuzha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, **Kerala Chief Minister**, launched his campaign in Alappuzha on Wednesday, April 1, 2026. He criticized **G. Sudhakaran**, a dissident CPI(M) veteran running as an Independent candidate, accusing him of aligning with the Congress and BJP for political gain.  **Vijayan** argued that Sudhakaran's actions were motivated by proving his worth to his new backers and tarnishing his former comrades. He also referenced past challenges faced by the CPI(M) in Alappuzha, suggesting a strong party-first approach among voters.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Election LIVE: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin to campaign in Coimbatore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister M.K. Stalin** will campaign in Coimbatore on April 2 for candidates contesting in the seven Assembly constituencies in the district. The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** released its manifesto for the April 9 Assam Assembly elections, promising to implement a Uniform Civil Code and protect indigenous people's land, heritage, and dignity. Meanwhile, **Rahul Gandhi** continued his campaign targeting **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan**, invoking the Sabarimala gold theft case and alleged deals between the CPI(M) and BJP.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election 2026: Polls heat up as major fronts step up campaigns and identity politics takes centrestage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: With the Kerala Assembly polls approaching, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra** are among the high-profile figures campaigning. The election has become increasingly polarized with accusations of backroom deals and communal overtures from groups like the SDPI and JIH.  The ruling **CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF)** is highlighting a decade of development, while the **United Democratic Front (UDF)** faces internal strife over its leadership and attempts to revive the Sabarimala gold theft scandal. The BJP seeks to expand its vote share into actual seats, but faces challenges from the FCRA issue with the Christian electorate.

recent_articles.title: UDF began preparations for Mission 2026 a year ago; it will win in Kerala: Satheesan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, believes the party will win the upcoming Kerala elections due to increased organizational preparedness and a groundswell of support from various social groups. He stated that he would resign from politics if the UDF does not achieve victory in the polls.  The UDF is confident of winning as they have successfully brought back 90% of the social groups who left the party, creating a broader political platform with diverse stakeholders. The CPI(M) is facing internal rebellion and losing its influence in Kerala, while the Congress has been working to improve its performance by addressing issues like price rise and gold pilferage at Sabarimala.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Pinarayi signals willingness to accept Satheesan’s challenge for a one-to-one debate on LDF governance - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** responded to **Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan's** challenge for a debate on the ten years of **LDF** governance by posting a progress report card highlighting achievements such as the Vizhinjam port project and land title distribution.  **Satheesan** criticized these claims as election-era hyperbole, demanding a face-to-face debate at a time and place chosen by **Vijayan**.  He also listed various issues he would address in the debate, including the CPI(M)-BJP electoral deal, the LDF's relationship with the SDPI, and the cost of living crisis.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: I have never received any pampering from media, says K.T. Jaleel - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Left Democratic Front (LDF) is pinning its hopes on K.T. Jaleel to retain the Tavanur Assembly seat in Malappuram district.  Jaleel, who served as Higher Education and Minority Welfare Minister in the first LDF government led by Pinarayi Vijayan, believes his strong bond with the people and the government's track record will secure his victory. He highlights several infrastructure projects implemented during his tenure, including bridges and flyovers, to demonstrate progress made in the constituency.  Jaleel faces a challenge from V.S. Joy of the Malappuram District Congress Committee.
